repository_object_identity.subject: a Git object (commit, tree, blob, tag) inside one object database
repository_object_identity.computation: the object format's hash over a header '<type> <size>\0' plus the bytes
format_change_implication: a SHA-256 object format produces 64 hexadecimal object ids; a recorded 40-character id does not name an object in such a repository
the same bytes have different object ids in repositories with different object formats
a format change rewrites every object id; recorded ids must be re-derived and an old id never compared with a new one as one naming scheme
the format is read from the repository, never inferred from a digest length

content_digests.subject: a byte sequence, inside or outside the repository
content_digests.naming_rule: every record names the algorithm in the field name or in an adjacent digest_algorithm/hash_algorithm field; an unnamed digest is a recorded migration population
content_digests.relationship_to_object_identity: none: a content digest can be computed without Git and an object id cannot

signature_and_attestation.statement: no DSSE envelope, Rekor entry, Sigstore bundle, OpenPGP signature or trusted timestamp exists in this repository; Addendum B is a work queue. No signature or attestation algorithm is therefore admitted, recorded or claimed
signature_and_attestation.non_claim: the absence of signatures is not evidence of integrity, and this item does not create one

digest_renewal.rule: a new authenticated commitment over the same archived bytes, preserving the old binding rather than replacing it

records.subject: evidence/etp0/CLAIMS.json
records.renewal_reason: demonstration of a digest-agility binding; no algorithm is being retired by this record
records.trusted_time_assumption: the renewal inherits the trust placed in the original record's time and does not retroactively establish it; the original timestamp and the renewal time are both recorded
records.statement: old and new digests are computed over the same archived bytes; the old binding is preserved rather than replaced, and the object id is recorded separately because it is not a content digest

records.subject: forensics/etp6/verify.sh
records.renewal_reason: demonstration of a digest-agility binding; no algorithm is being retired by this record
records.trusted_time_assumption: the renewal inherits the trust placed in the original record's time and does not retroactively establish it; the original timestamp and the renewal time are both recorded
records.statement: old and new digests are computed over the same archived bytes; the old binding is preserved rather than replaced, and the object id is recorded separately because it is not a content digest

what_a_renewal_cannot_do: it cannot retroactively prove that an old signature was valid before a compromise
it cannot change a repository object id
it cannot establish the original timestamp; it inherits trust in it

distinctness_evidence.statement: both values identify the same bytes and are not interchangeable: the object id is the repository format's hash over the object header plus the bytes, while the content digest is SHA-256 over the raw bytes

separation_rules: an object format is read from the repository with git rev-parse --show-object-format
a record that names an object format different from the observed one is refused (PM_IDENTITY_OBJECT_FORMAT_MISMATCH)
a content digest is named by its field; its length never implies an object format
a renewal binds two content-digest algorithms over identical bytes and records the object id separately
no signature or attestation algorithm is recorded while the system is absent
